question.worked_solution:
First, we write $1\,\frac{1}{9}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{1}{9}=\frac{(1\times 9)+1}{9}=\frac{10}{9}
$$

Also, we write $-\frac{1}{3}$ as $-\frac{3}{9}$ and then we simply subtract the numerators. This gives

$$
-\frac{3}{9}-\frac{10}{9}=\frac{-3-10}{9}.
$$

Now, we work out $-3-10$ using a number line:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14148354/assets/f27b92c1bbd62f5cba5fc75a4205034a24fb0298e77a662d6c59203dd42a2760.png)

So, we get

$$
\frac{-3-10}{9}=\frac{-13}{9}=-\frac{13}{9}.
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
-\frac{13}{9}=-1\,\frac{4}{9}
$$
